record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.original_question: Does hypothesis (R4) hold? Here (R4) is the assertion that for an arbitrary field K, if F|K is an extension admitting a K-rational place, then K is existentially closed in F. The paper explains that local uniformization would imply (R4), and that (R4) would in turn yield decidability of the existential Lval(t)-theory of F_p((t)).

evidence.quote:
In the paper [2] the assumption that implication 1)⇒3) holds for arbitrary fields
K is called hypothesis (R4). Hence local uniformization implies (R4).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field and let $F\mid K$ be a field extension. A place of $F$ is a map $P:F\to L\cup\{\infty\}$ (with $L$ a field) that is a ring homomorphism on its valuation ring and sends every element outside the valuation ring to $\infty$. The place $P$ is said to be $K$-rational if $P$ is the identity on $K$ and the residue field $FP$ equals $K$ (so $P$ fixes $K$ pointwise and the image of its valuation ring under $P$ is exactly $K$). One says that $K$ is existentially closed in $F$ if every existential first-order sentence in the language of rings with parameters from $K$ that holds in $F$ already holds in $K$.

Hypothesis (R4) asserts: for every field $K$ and every field extension $F\mid K$, if $F\mid K$ admits a $K$-rational place, then $K$ is existentially closed in $F$.

Question: Does hypothesis (R4) hold?
artifact.status_search_result: Hypothesis (R4) is a known open problem in the model theory of valued fields, connected to local uniformization in positive characteristic and to the decidability of the existential theory of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$. Recent surveys and talks by Kuhlmann list it as an open problem; no proof or counterexample for arbitrary fields $K$ has been published.

status_evidence.title: The Algebra and Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses hypothesis (R4) in connection with local uniformization and existential closure under K-rational places.
status_evidence.claim: (R4) is treated as an open hypothesis whose validity would follow from local uniformization.

status_evidence.title: Franz-Viktor Kuhlmann's talks
status_evidence.snippet: Talks repeatedly discuss the open status of (R4) and its connections to decidability of the existential theory of F_p((t)).
status_evidence.claim: (R4) is presented as an open problem in current research talks.
